Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Financial Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Financial Group's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Risk Officer; Robert Hayes, Chief Credit Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Thomas Grant, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Financial Group delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Accelerating revenue growth
2. Improving profitability
3. Managing risk effectively
4. Investing in technology and innovation
5. Enhancing customer experience
6. Strengthening our brand
7. Delivering value to our shareholders.

To give you a sense of our momentum, we achieved record adjusted earnings per share of $2.12, up 15% year-over-year and beating consensus by 7 cents. Total revenues hit $18.4 billion, rising 11% from last year, powered by net interest income of $12.4 billion and robust non-interest income growth. Our loan portfolio expanded 8.2% to $285 billion, with strong contributions across commercial, consumer, and mortgage segments. Efficiency improved meaningfully to 54.2%, reflecting disciplined expense control, while credit quality stayed pristine. Capital remains robust at a CET1 ratio of 12.8%, supporting $3 billion in share repurchases and a proposed 12% dividend increase.

I will now turn the call over to David Patel to discuss our financial results in more detail.

David Patel:
Thank you, Michael, and good morning. UniBank Financial Group reported net income of $2.8 billion for the third quarter, or $2.12 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Let me start with an overview of our overall company performance highlights. In this standout quarter amid a dynamic macro backdrop, we showcased the resilience of our diversified operations and the returns from our digital investments. Revenues reached $18.4 billion, up 11% year-over-year and 4% from Q2, with net interest income setting a record at $12.4 billion thanks to an optimized balance sheet in the higher-rate regime. Our net interest margin widened 22 basis points sequentially to 3.65%, aided by steady deposit growth to $950 billion—up 6% annually—and strategic securities adjustments. We outperformed peers like JPMorgan and Bank of America on NII expansion.

Non-interest revenues, now 34% of the total and up from 30% a year ago, climbed 5% to $6.3 billion. Investment banking fees jumped 22% to $1.8 billion on a surge in M&A, including four mega-deals over $5 billion in tech and healthcare, such as a U.S.-Europe fintech merger. Trading in markets hit $2.1 billion, up 8%, capturing fixed-income volatility from Fed cues and equity gains from AI stocks. Wealth management AUM grew 12% to $950 billion, with 9% net inflows, especially from ultra-high-net-worth clients in Asia via our private banking.

Expenses were tightly managed, driving our efficiency ratio to 54.2% from 58.0% last year. Adjusted operating expenses rose just 3% to $9.7 billion, with $450 million in savings from digital shifts. Provisions for credit losses were $1.2 billion, or 28 basis points on loans, supported by stable unemployment. Non-performing loans edged to 0.85% and net charge-offs held at 0.45%.

By segment, consumer and commercial banking revenues grew 10% to $10.2 billion, with loans up 5% to $650 billion—auto and small business up 8% and 7% via our mobile app with 28 million users. Wealth and investment management rose 13% to $4.1 billion, boosted by our Apex Wealth 360 robo-hybrid platform attracting millennials. Institutional clients added $4.1 billion, up 9%, on treasury services amid FX swings.

Regionally, U.S. ops at 55% of revenues grew 12%, leveraging consumer resilience and Sunbelt CRE stabilization. Europe, 25% of mix, advanced 8% despite MiFID III, excelling in $15 billion YTD green bonds from London. Asia-Pacific hit a record $2.8 billion, up 14%, via Ant Group embedded finance onboarding 5 million wallets. Emerging markets at 8% exposure stay diversified in ASEAN and LatAm.

Tech-wise, gen AI in contact centers cut resolution times 35%, handling 40% autonomously, akin to Goldman Sachs' Marcus. Blockchain trade finance with IBM processed $2 billion near-real-time. We exceeded $100 billion sustainable lending early at $120 billion.

ROTC reached 18.2% from 16.1%, ROA 1.45%. For Q4, revenues eyed 8-10% up, EPS $2.05-$2.15, with diversified 45% recurring streams mitigating Fed cut and CRE risks.

Now, turning to net interest income trends in more depth. NII was $12.4 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year but down 1.8% quarter-over-quarter, with nine-month total at $37.2 billion, up 9.1%. YoY growth marked our sixth straight strong quarter, from higher rates: average earning assets up 4.5% to $1.07 trillion, C&I loans +6.2% on $18 billion originations, consumer +3.8%. Deposits grew 3.1% to $950 billion, core at 62%; NIM +25 bps to 3.45% as asset yields rose 62 bps to 5.42%, funding costs +48 bps to 2.10%, buffered by $45 billion fixed wholesale. Securities yielded 4.25%, duration 2.8 years.

QoQ, NIM dipped 10 bps from deposit shifts to CDs amid 5.2% MMF yields, beta at 95%; loans +1.2%, CRE down 2.1%; segments: consumer/wealth $4.2B (+6%/-3%), commercial $5.8B (+10%/flat), markets $2.4B (+4%/+2%). Regions: U.S. +9%, Europe +2%, APAC +12%.

Mitigants: AI deposit pricing retained $8 billion; $10 billion securities swaps; cross-sell. Q4 NII $12.5-12.8 billion, FY 8% growth, NIM 3.40-3.50%.

Next, loan growth by segment drove much of this. Average loans +8.2% YoY to $285 billion, beating FDIC peers. Commercial up 11.5% to $142 billion: C&I +14.2% on SaaS/tech/renewables ($4.2 billion originations, DSCR 1.8x), AI models with Dun & Bradstreet; CRE +7.8%, industrial +22% (LTV 62%), Midwest manufacturing $1.8 billion ESG. NCOs 12 bps.

Consumer +7.9% to $68 billion: auto +12.3% (FICO 735, $2.1 billion Southeast), cards +5.6% (Delta co-brand), personal +4.2% (Affirm BNPL $450 million); delinq 2.8%. Mortgage +3.4% to $75 billion: purchases +6.8% ($3.9 billion jumbo), MSRs $120 million; non-QM $850 million (Rocket tech), Sun Belt 42%.

LDR 88%, quantum blockchain next, API embedded $5 billion target. FY guide: commercial 11-12%, consumer 7-8%, mortgage 3-4%.

On operating expenses, non-interest expenses hit $9.7 billion, up 4.2% YoY but down 1.8% sequentially—yielding efficiency of 54.2% from 58.2%. Multi-year program delivered $450 million savings.

Compensation/benefits (42%) +6.1% to $1.20 billion: 4% salaries, talent retention, $75 million incentives (var comp 28%). Tech/data (22%) $627 million +8.7% YoY/-3% QoQ: AWS core 85% coverage ($120 million savings), gen AI Palantir/Snowflake ($50 million), cyber $180 million. Occupancy +3.5% $285 million (120 branch closures), prof/reg fees +12% $320 million (Basel IV/Dodd-Frank), marketing +2% $210 million (neo-app 8 million users).

Regions: NA 3% up, EMEA 7% (ring-fencing), APAC flat. Ahead: $600 million RPA/UiPath savings (35% processing), vendor cuts; FY 4-5% growth, efficiency to 55% 2025.

Our efficiency ratio progress reinforces this: 54.2% in Q3, +210 bps QoQ from 56.3%, +380 bps YoY from 58.0%; TTM 55.1%, better than JPM 55%, BofA/WF 57-59%. Expenses +2.1% to $9.7 billion vs revenue +8.4% to $18.4 billion. Branch cuts 120 ($85 million save), headcount -5%, Temenos 75% ($120 million mainframe cut), Google Vertex AI 40% review time save (30 bps), UniWealth AI $15B AUM.

Regions: NA 53.1% (NIM 3.85%), Europe 56.8% (DORA €45 million), APAC 52.9% (UPI/Alipay +25% QoQ). Reinvest $500 million fintech (Plaid/Stripe UniBizFlow for $2T B2B). FY target 53-54%, Q4 53.5-54.0%; sub-50% 2027 AI centers. CET1 $2.8B buffer.

For outlook on loan growth and credit quality: total loans +5.2% YoY to $285 billion; FY25 5-7% (up from 4-6%). C&I (42%, $120B) 7-9% (SOFR+225 Southeast), CRE (28%, $80B) 2-4% (industrial +6%, office cap $6.4B derisk $1.2B), resi/HE (18%, $51B) flat-2% (AI pre-approvals), consumer/auto (12%, $34B) 4-6% (FlexLine). Southeast 60% drives 70%.

Credit: CECL 1.25% ($3.6B), NPL 72 bps, NCO 28 bps (2025 35-45 bps), provisions $900M-$1.1B. ML scoring (Experian), diversif (healthcare 18%), rel banking 65%. Sensit: cuts +1-2% growth/-5 bps NIM.

Finally, risk-weighted assets management: RWAs $482 billion, -1.8% QoQ/-4.2% YoY, density 42%. Credit 78% $376B -2.3% (wholesale -3.1% oil/gas derisk), market $28B -5.2% (hedging), op $52B -1%, CCR $26B flat. Regions: NA $313B -2.5% (CCAR), Europe $105B -3.8%, APAC $87B +1.2%. Tech: Moody's Axis sim $15B relief, $8B securit (auto ABS), ECL climate. FY25 2-3% growth, ROTE 15-18%.

Our capital ratios remain strong, and we are well-positioned to support future growth.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, David. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring commercial real estate pressures, deposit beta shifts amid rate uncertainty, and cybersecurity threats in a tense geopolitical climate. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks, including advanced loss modeling, portfolio diversification, and zero-trust enhancements, maintaining a strong risk profile with CET1 buffer over 250 bps in stress scenarios.

Robert Hayes:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains exceptionally strong with non-performing loans at 72 basis points and net charge-offs at 28 basis points. We are actively managing our loan portfolio across commercial, consumer, and mortgage segments and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment. Specifically, the performance of our commercial real estate portfolio has been managed prudently, with derisking in office and focus on industrial.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation, including the launch of our Temenos Transact core platform migration—now 75% complete—which has reduced processing costs 22%, and generative AI via Google Cloud Vertex for onboarding and fraud, cutting times 40%. UniWealth AI with BlackRock Aladdin scales efficiently, alongside AWS cloud shifts and UiPath RPA.

Thomas Grant:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include our network optimization closing 120 branches for $85 million savings while expanding digital hubs, and gen AI orchestration in contact centers for 30% labor reductions, contributing to improved productivity and cost savings.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide further insights into the efficiency ratio progress and targets?

David Patel:
Absolutely, John. Our efficiency ratio of 54.2% marks a 210 basis point sequential gain and 380 year-over-year, with TTM at 55.1% leading peers. This stems from expense growth of 2.1% versus 8.4% revenue, branch optimizations saving $85 million, headcount trims offset by analytics hires, Temenos savings, Vertex AI contributing 30 bps, and regional wins like APAC's sub-1% digital costs. FY target 53-54%, long-term sub-50% via AI, with reinvestments in Plaid/Stripe for B2B capture.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for loan growth outlook amid potential Fed cuts?

David Patel:
Thanks, Emily. We're guiding 5-7% total growth in 2025, led by C&I 7-9% on sponsor/middle-market in Texas/Florida, CRE 2-4% selective multifamily/industrial, consumer 4-6% auto/HELOC, mortgages flat-2%. Tech like FIS/nCino AI underwriting boosts speed/accuracy; ESG $5 billion target. Credit stays strong, NCOs 35-45 bps, with diversif and ML mitigants.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
How are you managing risk-weighted assets and CRE exposure?

Lisa Chen:
Good question, Mike. RWAs down 1.8% QoQ to $482 billion, density 42%, via credit derisking like $12 billion oil/gas, securitizations $8 billion, model approvals. CRE office capped, derisked $1.2 billion; climate ECL pilots add minimal PD. CET1 12.8% supports growth, with Basel IV floors simulated for $15 billion relief.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Laura Kim:
Can you discuss the performance of your commercial loan segment?

Robert Hayes:
Sure, Laura. Commercial loans grew 11.5% to $142 billion, C&I +14.2% on $4.2 billion SaaS/renewables originations with strong DSCRs and AI risk models; CRE +7.8% industrial-focused, Midwest CHIPS $1.8 billion ESG. Credit pristine at 12 bps NCOs, LTVs tight, regional balance.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Michael Reynolds for any closing remarks.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
